items.q: Design a pipeline ingesting fundamentals from 50 sources daily, serving batch analytics and a near-real-time dashboard.
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Three layers: (1) Ingestion -- NiFi fetches data and lands raw files in S3, config-driven per source. (2) Processing -- Spark validates types and business rules; invalid records go to dead-letter S3 with alerts; valid records become Parquet partitioned by date. (3) Serving -- Spark batch jobs query processed data for full analytics; pre-aggregated daily rollups feed the dashboard so it does not hit the heavy pipeline on every page load.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** EF Core builds an Expression Tree, translates it via the relational SQL provider into a parameterized T-SQL query, and materializes entities into the DbContext Change Tracker. N+1 queries occur when navigating un-included navigation properties in a loop.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Executing queries without AsNoTracking() in read-only APIs forces EF Core to keep snapshot copies of all returned entities in memory, causing high RAM usage and CPU tracking overhead.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** AsNoTracking() speeds up read queries by 20-30% and reduces memory footprint, but disables identity resolution and automatic change tracking for updates.

items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Config-driven: store per-source metadata in a config table (DynamoDB or S3 JSON) -- URL, auth, format, schema, validation rules, schedule. The ingestion code reads this at runtime and operates generically. Adding source 51 is adding a config row. Zero code changes, zero deploy.

items.q: What is idempotency and why is it essential?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** An idempotent pipeline produces the same result regardless of how many times it runs on the same input. Re-running today's pipeline should not duplicate records. Implement via mode('overwrite') on Parquet partitions, MERGE statements in SQL, date-partitioned output paths. Enables safe reruns -- how you fix bugs without corrupting data.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Async methods compile into an IAsyncStateMachine struct managed by the AsyncMethodBuilder. Awaiting an uncompleted task yields execution back to the caller. Blocking with .Result on a thread bound to a SynchronizationContext causes deadlocks when the continuation waits for the blocked thread.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Sync-over-async (.Result or .Wait()) on ASP.NET request threads rapidly exhausts thread pool threads, leading to HTTP 503 gateway timeouts and request queuing under load.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Async all the way preserves thread pool scalability, but requires passing CancellationToken through all layers and avoiding sync blocking methods everywhere.

items.q: How would you version a dataset schema without breaking existing consumers?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Additive (new nullable columns): Parquet handles automatically -- existing readers see null. Breaking changes: new versioned path (v2/) that new consumers opt into while old consumers stay on v1, or a transition period where both field names coexist before deprecating the old one on a communicated timeline. Never break consumers without a migration path.

items.q: How do you test transformation logic without running the full dataset?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Create a representative test dataset: 10-20 rows covering edge cases (nulls, duplicates, boundary values). Write unit tests: given this input, assert this output. pytest + assert_frame_equal for pandas; local SparkSession for PySpark. Test the function in isolation -- integration tests on full pipelines live separately as slower tests.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** SQL Server compiles T-SQL into an execution plan based on statistics histogram estimates. Parameter sniffing occurs when a plan compiled for a specific parameter (e.g. 1 row) is reused for a parameter matching 1,000,000 rows, leading to index scan or memory grant spills.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Implicit datatype conversion (e.g. passing NVARCHAR parameter to VARCHAR indexed column) forces SQL Server to run CONVERT() on every row, turning index seeks into full index scans.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** READ COMMITTED SNAPSHOT (RCSI) eliminates reader-writer blocking using tempdb row versioning, but increases tempdb I/O and version store management overhead.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Angular Signals maintain an internal reactive dependency graph (ReactiveNode). When a signal value updates, it marks dependent computed nodes as stale without running change detection immediately. Evaluation happens lazily when read, updating only impacted DOM bindings.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Writing to signals inside an effect() can trigger infinite reactive loops or untracked state dependencies. Fix: use computed() or linkedSignal() for derived state sync, keeping effect() strictly for un-tracked side effects like logging or localStorage.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Signals provide fine-grained, synchronous reactivity without Zone.js overhead, but require learning new primitives (input(), output(), model()) compared to classic RxJS BehaviorSubjects.
